title: Club Membership: enrollment fee calculation order and rounding
content:
## Scope
This document states how the Club Membership enrollment fee's employer-funded reduction, where one applies, actually combines with the tier's own original enrollment fee amount to produce the billed amount.

## Rule
The combined reduction percentage is applied once, directly to the tier's own original enrollment fee amount; it is never applied in successive steps and never applied to any amount other than that original tier figure. The amount actually billed is rounded to 2 decimal places only at the end of this calculation, with no intermediate rounding, and the billed amount is never a negative figure.

## Worked example (hypothetical)
Suppose a tier's own original enrollment fee amount is $49.00, and the member's linked employer partnership tier's own discount percentage combined with that same partnership tier's own multi-location discount percentage adds up, hypothetically, to a combined 15 percent. The billed enrollment fee is $49.00 reduced by 15 percent of itself, giving $41.65, rounded to 2 decimal places. This example's 15 percent is illustrative only, not a fixed figure of this policy.

## Points of judgement
The combined percentage is never applied twice in sequence (once for each of its two components) against a shrinking base; it is applied exactly once, as a single combined percentage, to the tier's own unreduced original enrollment fee amount. Where no reduction applies at all, the billed amount is simply the tier's own original enrollment fee amount, rounded to 2 decimal places.
